---
title: "Hands-on Exercise 4"
subtitle: "First-order Spatial Point Patterns Analysis"
---

This exercise studies the intensity and broad spatial distribution of point events using nearest-neighbour methods and kernel density estimation (KDE).

::: {.chapter-link}
[Open the course reference for Chapter 4](https://r4gdsa.netlify.app/chap04.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}
:::

## Learning focus

- Import, wrangle, and validate event and study-area data.
- Prepare point-pattern objects for analysis.
- Apply the Clark–Evans nearest-neighbour test.
- Estimate spatial intensity with kernel density estimation.
- Compare fixed and adaptive bandwidth approaches.
- Produce a cartographically clear KDE map.
- Summarise first-order patterns at planning-subzone level.

## Analysis workflow

1. Define the study area and clean the point-event data.
2. Confirm that the coordinate system is suitable for distance-based analysis.
3. Examine nearest-neighbour structure.
4. Estimate and compare density surfaces.
5. Interpret where event intensity is relatively high or low, with attention to boundary effects and bandwidth choice.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
First-order methods describe intensity across space; they do not by themselves establish why a pattern occurs.
:::
